title: Thrown into show drumming; Buddy Rich at the DeLisa
summary: Learning shows by being thrown in, a similar story from DeMichael, and Buddy Rich watching him play the DeLisa show.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Okay. So you started -- that's when you started playing shows.
That's when I started doing shows. That was my first introduction. And so I really didn't --
really wasn't -- it wasn't a gradual thing. I was just thrown into -- the rabbit in the briar patch.
Yeah, that happened to me, too. I was playing in this band, we got a show, and there was a pretty tough show --
Really screwed up. So I got me a job in a strip joint.
And learned to play shows. And by the time I left Louisville, I was --
I was one of the guys they called when they had a job to play.
Right. And then after that I played many a nightclub, but they were all joints to me. I had really cut my teeth already, so it was no problem anymore.
Yeah. Buddy Rich made a very nice statement in a recent DownBeat, that when he played Chicago, he'd always get out to DeLisa to watch you play the show.

Yeah, right, right. And he used to come out -- but -- and I remember it so much. And I had a picture, but I turned a lot of valuable and beautiful pictures over to the Chicago Historical Society. And I think they've got this picture of Buddy and myself in there, and then he was a young guy and I was real young. And that was some years ago,
I remember those pictures in DownBeat of you for -- what was it, Slingeland
Yeah, Slingeland Drum Company, yeah, right, yes, sir.
